content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn introduction to amazon ec2 in the context of Amazon EC2 and Virtual Servers. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: Introduction to Amazon EC2 matters because it is one part of amazon ec2 and virtual servers. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** Introduction to Amazon EC2 belongs to Amazon EC2 and Virtual Servers. EC2 is a flexible virtual-server option. Safe operation includes image hygiene, least-privilege instance roles, patching, persistent-storage awareness, monitoring and cleanup.

The PDF lists these subtopics: What EC2 provides; Virtual servers in the cloud; EC2 use cases; EC2 compared with managed compute services. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For introduction to amazon ec2, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: What EC2 provides
items.text: Identify the AWS resource or design decision involved, the permissions and prerequisites it needs, and the evidence that shows it is configured as intended.

items.title: Virtual servers in the cloud
items.text: Compare the available option with the workload requirement; record the operational, security, availability and cost trade-offs rather than assuming one option is always best.

items.title: EC2 use cases
items.text: Write a verification step and a failure case. For hands-on work, start with read-only inspection and use an approved sandbox before changing cloud resources.

items.title: EC2 compared with managed compute services
items.text: Record ownership, dependencies and teardown/recovery behavior so the design can be operated safely after the first successful test.

content_blocks.title: Inventory instance states: Introduction to Amazon EC2

aws ec2 describe-instances --query "Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,State.Name,InstanceType]" --output table

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use least privilege, keep Block Public Access/private defaults unless a justified reviewed requirement says otherwise, and document cost/cleanup before live changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.
